findings.pattern: local encodeJson + per-command JSON-encode error wrappers
findings.description: The line `const encodeJson = S.encodeUnknownEffect(S.UnknownFromJsonString)` is re-declared in 12 files, each then wrapping it in its own error-mapped `encodeCommandJson`/`renderJson` (Yeet.renderJson, AIMetrics.encodeCommandJson, Docgen variants). internal/cli/Json.ts already defines the encoder plus an `encodeCommandJson`, but keeps it private and hard-codes CliJsonError, so every command rolled its own with its command error tag.
findings.proposedHome: packages/tooling/tool/cli/src/internal/cli/Json.ts — export encodeCommandJson returning Effect<string, ParseError> (or CliJsonError) so callers attach their own mapError; delete the 12 local re-declarations

findings.pattern: two independent ASCII progress-bar renderers (Files vs Image)
findings.description: Files.progress.ts and Image.render.ts+Image.progress.ts each implement the same TTY-guarded, single-line, in-place `#`/`-` progress bar with percent `.toFixed(1)`, terminal.display, and completion newline — ~215 LOC vs ~130 LOC of parallel code (bar fill math, clear-line/`\r` redraw, `process.stdout.isTTY === true` gate, event-to-render dispatch). Only styling (chalk/colors vs plain) and event source differ.
findings.proposedHome: packages/tooling/tool/cli/src/internal/cli/Progress.ts — shared bar renderer (width, label, completed/total or percent, optional color) + TTY-gated in-place display combinator; Files/Image keep thin domain adapters

findings.pattern: jsonc pretty-print renderJson with 500k cap, duplicated verbatim
findings.description: Three Docgen internal files contain byte-identical `renderJson` (encodeJson -> jsonc.format tabSize 2 -> applyEdits, skip when > JSON_FORMAT_MAX_LENGTH) plus three identical `const JSON_FORMAT_MAX_LENGTH = 500_000` constants; Docgen.command.ts:218 has a fourth near-identical copy without the cap. Only the error message string differs.
findings.proposedHome: packages/tooling/tool/cli/src/internal/cli/Json.ts — add `renderPrettyCommandJson(value, { maxFormatLength })` next to printCommandJson

findings.pattern: if (json) print encoded JSON else printLines — hand-rolled per subcommand
findings.description: The dual-output branch `if (json) { yield* Console.log(yield* xToJson(v)); return } ... printLines([...])` is re-written at every subcommand handler: 27 branch sites in AIMetrics alone, plus dual-signature render* wrappers in AgentEffectiveness and repeats in Docgen, Files, Quality, Yeet. Each site re-plumbs the same encode-then-log vs lines fallback shape.
findings.existingHelper: packages/tooling/tool/cli/src/internal/cli/Json.ts printCommandJson + internal/cli/Printer.ts printLines (halves exist, combinator does not)
findings.proposedHome: packages/tooling/tool/cli/src/internal/cli/Printer.ts — `printJsonOrLines(json: boolean, value: unknown, lines: () => ReadonlyArray<string>)` (or match-based) composing printCommandJson and printLines

findings.pattern: [tag] prefixed log lines and [tag] key=value summary blocks
findings.description: ~130 `Console.log(`[tag] ...`)` lines across ~18 files hand-interpolate a bracketed command prefix (20 distinct tags: [schema-first], [yeet], [dual-arity], [dry-run], [graphiti-*], [effect-governance-*], ...), including multi-line key=value summary blocks (18 consecutive lines in SchemaFirst, 4 blocks in Laws.command.ts). No shared prefixed-logger or tagged-summary renderer exists.
findings.proposedHome: packages/tooling/tool/cli/src/internal/cli/Printer.ts — `makeTaggedLogger(tag)` returning line/summary printers, plus `logTaggedSummary(tag, record)` for key=value blocks

findings.pattern: jsonFlag re-declared despite shared internal/cli/Flags.ts jsonFlag

QualityArtifactSupport.discoverWorkspacePackages and Quality/Tasks.workspaceTaskOwners additionally need manifests/scripts, which resolveWorkspaceDirs does not return — the gap that drives the copies.

findings.pattern: findRepoRoot() + per-command 'Failed to locate repository root' mapError
findings.description: The exact composition findRepoRoot().pipe(XCommandError.mapError("Failed to locate repository root.")) recurs ~25 times, including 10+ times inside Quality.command.ts alone where the root could be resolved once per handler. Thin per-line duplication but a hotspot for hoisting rather than a new helper.

findings.description: Three complete reimplementations of the same ratchet lifecycle: read committed JSONC baseline, compute current findings/totals, diff (introduced/increased, resolved/decreased, missing), enforce with '[tag] regression:' stderr block + tagged error exit 1, '[tag] ok:' line, '[tag] tighten-baseline:' nudge, and a --write-baseline mode that regenerates the document with schema_version/regeneration_command header. The Laws/Lint inventory verifiers (missing/stale drift + merge + write mode) are the same shape a fourth and fifth time; KnipRatchet carries explicit fallow-ignore code-duplication markers.
findings.proposedHome: packages/tooling/tool/cli/src/internal/ratchet/ (generic Ratchet.make parameterized by finding schema, equivalence/order, renderers, tag, and regeneration commands)

findings.description: Every ratchet/inventory file privately rebuilds readBaseline (resolve repo-relative path -> readFileString -> mapError 'Failed to read X' -> JSONC/JSON schema decode -> mapError 'Failed to decode X') and writeBaseline (makeDirectory dirname recursive -> formatJsonc/jsonStringifyPretty/renderBiomeJson -> prepend '// Do not edit by hand / Regenerate with:' header -> writeFileString with trailing newline), differing only in the tagged error class. Quality's readJsonc/readText/formatJsonc in QualityArtifactSupport are group-private, so Laws/Lint/AgentEffectiveness re-derive the same code.
findings.proposedHome: packages/tooling/tool/cli/src/internal/artifacts/ArtifactIo.ts (readArtifact(schema, path)/writeArtifact(schema, path, doc, headerLines) generic over the caller's tagged error via a mapError hook); promote formatJsonc there from Quality/internal/QualityArtifactSupport.ts
findings.existingHelper: partial: decodeJsoncTextAs (@beep/schema/Jsonc), jsonStringifyPretty + renderBiomeJson (packages/tooling/library/repo-utils), formatJsonc/readJsonc (packages/tooling/tool/cli/src/commands/Quality/internal/QualityArtifactSupport.ts, group-private)

findings.description: KnipRatchet.parseJsonc and DualArity.readInventoryDocument both re-implement jsonc-parser parse(text, parseErrors, {allowTrailingComma, disallowComments:false}) plus ParseError formatting, while decodeJsoncTextAs in @beep/schema/Jsonc already does parse+decode and is used by JSDocRatchet/CoverageRegression/FallowFeedback. SchemaFirst.readInventoryDocument uses bare parse(content) with no error capture and Effect.option, silently swallowing corrupt-inventory parse failures.
findings.proposedHome: existing helper

N more' suffix), differing only in the per-item render function; KnipRatchet marks it with a fallow-ignore code-duplication comment.

findings.description: An identical `renderJson` — `S.encodeUnknownEffect(S.UnknownFromJsonString)` then `jsonc.format`/`jsonc.applyEdits` with a 500_000-char `JSON_FORMAT_MAX_LENGTH` compact-fallback — is copied verbatim into three Docgen eval modules plus Docgen.command.ts/Operations.ts, and the same uncapped jsonc pretty-print recurs in Skills, TsconfigSync, and SyncDataToTs. internal/cli/Json.ts only offers compact `printCommandJson`, so every eval report re-implements stable pretty rendering.

findings.pattern: schema-first policy finding wire schema triplicated
findings.description: The JSON-line finding emitted by `beep lint schema-first` is modeled three times: SchemaFirstPolicyFinding (emitter), SchemaFirstPolicyOutput (Yeet consumer), and SchemaFirstPolicyIssue (AgentEffectiveness consumer), each decoded via S.fromJsonString. They have already diverged: EvalScorer types severity as optional S.String and remediation as optional, while the emitter requires QualityIssueSeverity/SchemaFirstPolicySeverity and a required remediation, so producer/consumer drift is silent.

findings.description: The pair `S.withConstructorDefault(Effect.succeed(x)) + S.withDecodingDefault(Effect.succeed(x))` with the same value is hand-rolled ~40+ times for empty-array defaults alone (140 withConstructorDefault / 112 withDecodingDefault occurrences package-wide), while @beep/schema SchemaUtils.withKeyDefaults exists for exactly this and is already used 24 times in the same package. Caveat: withKeyDefaults uses withDecodingDefaultTypeKey (decoded-value default); sites that intentionally supply Encoded defaults (e.g. A.empty<Entry.Encoded>()) need per-site verification.
findings.proposedHome: @beep/schema SchemaUtils.withKeyDefaults (existing); optionally a tiny `defaultedArray(schema)` wrapper in packages/tooling/tool/cli/src/internal/cli/ for the empty-array case

findings.description: The same three-mode execution domain is defined three ways: VersionSyncModeKit = LiteralKit(["check","write","dry-run"]), SyncDataRunModeKit = LiteralKit(["write","check","dry-run"]), and Skills uses a plain TS union `type SkillsRunMode = "write" | "check" | "dry-run"` (LiteralKit law violation). The flags-to-mode resolveMode(check, dryRun) helper is also duplicated in Skills.command.ts:829 and VersionSync.command.ts:30.
findings.proposedHome: packages/tooling/tool/cli/src/internal/cli/RunMode.ts (shared LiteralKit + flag-resolution helper, next to Flags.ts)

findings.pattern: lint/quality severity literal kits duplicated and divergent
findings.description: LiteralKit(["warning","error"]) is defined identically in Lint/SchemaFirst.ts and Lint/ReflectionArtifact.ts; Laws/NoNativeRuntime.ts uses the divergent spelling ["warn","error"]; Yeet's QualityIssueSeverity is the superset ["info","warning","error","fatal"]. @beep/schema SeverityLevel (low/medium/high/critical) is a different domain and does not cover this; a shared lint-severity kit would kill the warn/warning drift.
findings.proposedHome: packages/tooling/tool/cli/src/internal/quality/Severity.ts (shared LiteralKit; QualityIssueSeverity superset can live beside it or derive the two-member kit as a subset)

findings.pattern: ISO timestamp fields modeled as bare S.String
findings.description: 12 report/document schema fields (generatedAt, createdAt, startedAt, generatedOn, timestamp, generated_at) are typed as bare S.String even though @beep/schema exports a validated ISOStr (Timestamp module) that repo-cli can use directly; nothing rejects a non-ISO value today. The companion runtime idiom `DateTime.now.pipe(Effect.map(DateTime.formatIso))` is also repeated ~12 times plus two private `timestampIso` consts in Docgen internals.
findings.proposedHome: @beep/schema ISOStr for the schema fields; a shared `nowIso` Effect in packages/tooling/tool/cli/src/internal/cli/ for the runtime idiom

findings.description: TsconfigSync defines branded BeepScopedPackageName (isStartsWith "@beep/") and CreatePackage defines branded PackageName (regex), while @beep/repo-utils (already a repo-cli dependency) exports NpmPackageName and RepoPackageName with stricter validated patterns; additionally ~14 schema files carry unvalidated `packageName: S.String` fields that could adopt RepoPackageName.

findings.description: The field set `message: S.String, command?: S.optionalKey(S.String), exitCode?: S.optionalKey(S.Finite), cause?: S.optionalKey(S.Defect({includeStack:true}))` plus the identical `override [Runtime.errorExitCode] = this.exitCode ?? 1` is repeated across at least 8 <Group>.errors.ts tagged errors (Worktree, Yeet, Graphiti, Codex, Quality x2, plus internals). A shared field-spread constant would remove the copy-paste while keeping per-group tags.

findings.pattern: count fields as S.Finite instead of NonNegativeInt
findings.description: Ratchet/quality summary schemas model counts (finding totals, severity_*_count, line counts) as bare S.Finite, which admits negative and fractional values, while @beep/schema NonNegativeInt is already imported by 9 other files in the same package (Research, Corpus, Files, FallowQuality). KnipRatchet alone has 17 S.Finite fields and Docgen Quality 15.
findings.proposedHome: @beep/schema NonNegativeInt (existing); apply where the field is semantically a count (exit codes and percentages excluded)
